_: READ OFF .rip/mario/bands/band_NN.png BY EYE. See spriteforge/rip.py for why
this is hand-authored: caption left-edges align with some tile left-edge for
134 of 430 cells, so an automatic split fires three times too often and every
false fire puts frames in the wrong move silently.
`facings` maps a facing to an index into the BAND'S OWN row list. On this
sheet a captioned band holds the same poses twice: row 0 seen from the front,
row 1 seen from behind. So one column range names the move in both facings.
Band 0 is the 'Common' section, 22 columns:
idle 0-1 · tired idle 2-4 · walk/run 5-7 · before jump 8-9 · jump 10-11
fall 12-13 · spin jump 14 · spin fall 15 · spin land 16-18 · sit 19
squish 20-21
Band 6 is 'Smash', where only columns 0 and 4 are Mario — 1-3 are the hammer
props and 5-7 are the coin burst.
`mirror` because this art FACES LEFT. `dir` is a promise about the screen —
E means seen walking right — and animator.ts renders W as E flipped. With no
E sheet, E falls back to S, so left-facing art made BOTH directions wrong:
walking right showed his back-of-nose, and walking left flipped him to face
right. Declaring the mirror fixes both at once.
`roll` is Space — the dodge (player.ts plays 'roll', and the wall-launch hop
reuses the same art). Spin Jump / Spin Fall / Spin Land is a real tumble arc,
which is what a dodge roll wants; the plain Jump/Fall pair is not.
`ball` is the PLUNGER RIDE — hold Space and you launch as a marble, which
was the knight's painted ball. Band 1 columns 3-7 are Spin, Speedy Spin and
Spin Attack: five frames of Mario spinning, which is the closest thing to a
roll a sheet of a man who does not curl into a ball can offer.
The six MATERIAL marbles (steelball, diamondball, waterball, stoneball,
stormball, lavaball) and the two ricochet forms stay PAINTED on purpose. The
marble you are riding is a gameplay signal — a diamond has to read as
diamond — and a spinning Mario in place of it would trade information for
novelty. Only the plain `ball` becomes him.
`death` is Fall Down (17, 18) into Fallen (2). A death clip has to END on a
rest pose or the corpse keeps twitching; 2 is Mario lying still.
Band 1 has ONE tile row, so these three clips are authored once and every
facing reuses them — see frames_for in character.py. A spin and a corpse read
the same from either side.
NO `run`. This sheet's caption is literally 'Walk / Run' — one animation for
both — so publishing run:[5,6,7] made it a byte-identical copy of walk, which
mislabel.test.ts rejects (IoU 0.95 / dcolour 20). It is right to: two clip
rows that are the same pixels mean one of them is mislabelled. The reuse now
happens at RUNTIME instead — see `alias()` in render/imported-paints.ts — so
Mario sprints as Mario, at the run frame rate, with no duplicated pixels.
